title: A work order invoiced with nobody takes the customer's reps per side
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have two active staff members at the test location with their "Sales Representative" switch on: sales rep A and sales rep B.
  • Use a customer with "Sales Representative - Service Labor" set to sales rep A and "Sales Representative - Service Parts" set to sales rep B.
  • Have a work order for that customer with one labor line of $100.00 and one part of $50.00, with both sides reading "Unassigned", and invoice it today without picking a representative.
  • Open Reports > Sales By Representative in a desktop browser at least 1024 pixels wide, with the date range set to today and the Sales Type column turned on.
custom_steps:
1. Expand sales rep A.
  2. Expand sales rep B.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The labor of the work order's invoice ($100.00) is credited to sales rep A on a "Labor" row.

Step 2:

  • The part ($50.00) is credited to sales rep B on a "Parts" row.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11268 (Story 4, Give a customer default representatives), story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S4-R17: “A work order invoiced with nobody on either side is credited with the customer's Service Parts person on the parts side and the Service Labor person on the labor side. A customer that is not split gives its one person both sides.”
  • S5-R3: “The report reads every invoice as one row per representative per Sales Type: "Labor" for a work order's labor side, "Parts" for its parts side, and "Part Sales" for a part sale.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
